facts.raw_span: painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis of 1 month's duration
elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy discovered 9 years prior
fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite
asymptomatic 'green-yellow welts' and swelling of the glans penis
swelling became progressively painful and evolved to the size of an 'orange' over 4 days
no improvement with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin
glans penis and corona were grossly edematous
3.7 × 3.3-cm tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar, adherent yellow crust, and granulation tissue
no urethral discharge was present
routine blood test results were within normal limits
dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes, which were CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, within the background of a reactive T-cell infiltrate
clonal IgH gene rearrangement

concepts.why: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement and expression of CD20, CD79a, and CD5 is consistent with a diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
The presence of a reactive T-cell infiltrate and atypical lymphocytes in the skin lesion could suggest a diagnosis of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
The presence of a destructive skin lesion with atypical lymphocytes and a clonal IgH gene rearrangement could suggest a diagnosis of extramodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma.
The presence of a lymphoma in the penis, which is a rare site for lymphoma, could suggest a diagnosis of primary penile lymphoma.
The presence of swelling, pain, and warmth in the skin, which are characteristic features of cellulitis, could suggest a diagnosis of bacterial cellulitis.
The presence of a skin lesion with a history of swelling and pain, which are characteristic features of eczema herpeticum, could suggest a diagnosis of eczema herpeticum.
The presence of a skin lesion with a history of swelling and pain, which are characteristic features of folliculitis, could suggest a diagnosis of bacterial folliculitis.
The presence of a skin lesion with a history of swelling and pain, which are characteristic features of a penile ulcer, could suggest a diagnosis of penile ulcer.

rationales.F01: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis is more typical of lymphoma or penile ulcer than other options.
rationales.F08: The presence of a large, tender ulcer with black eschar and granulation tissue is highly suggestive of a malignant process such as lymphoma.
rationales.F11: The dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes with specific immunophenotyping is diagnostic of B-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F12: The clonal IgH gene rearrangement is a specific marker for B-cell lymphoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The biopsy of the glans penis ulcer showed dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes, which were CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, and PCR analysis revealed a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, supporting the diagnosis of Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
